title: Lease Renewal Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free lease renewal letter template: offer a tenant a new fixed term or month-to-month extension with updated rent and terms.
lead: A letter from a landlord to a tenant offering to renew their lease for a new fixed term (often 12 months) or on a month-to-month basis, with any updated terms and rent.
introParagraphs: A lease renewal letter is sent to a tenant toward the end of their fixed-term lease offering to extend the tenancy. It states the new term, any rent change, and any updated rules or clauses.

If the tenant signs and returns the renewal (or a new lease is executed), the tenancy continues under the new terms. If the tenant declines or does not respond by the deadline, the lease typically rolls to month-to-month per local law or ends as written.
bullets: Tenant and property
Tenant name, property address and unit number, current lease dates.
New term
Renewal term length (e.g. 12 months) and new start/end dates, or a switch to month-to-month.
Rent change
New monthly rent amount, effective date, and the reason (market rate, CPI, property taxes) — some jurisdictions require specific notice and justification.
Changes to terms
Any new clauses or updates (pet policy, utilities, late fees, maintenance responsibilities).
Response deadline
Date by which the tenant must sign and return or give notice to vacate.
howTo: Check local notice rules
Most areas require renewal/non-renewal notices 30-90 days before lease end; some rent-controlled areas require more.
Decide terms early
Confirm rent, term length and any policy changes before drafting.
Send the letter
Mail or email per the lease notice clause; keep a signed/dated copy and proof of delivery.
Get a signed response
Ask the tenant to sign and return by the deadline, or sign a new lease.
Handle non-response
If the tenant does not respond, follow local law — typically the lease goes month-to-month or the tenant must vacate.
related: When renewing with a rent change, a standalone notice may be required.
Mutual agreement to end the lease instead of renewing.
Non-renewal notice when a tenant or landlord is ending the tenancy.
The new lease for the renewal term.
faq: Do I have to offer a renewal?
In most places no — unless rent control or local ordinance requires it. You can choose not to renew with proper notice.
How much notice is required?
Typically 30-60 days before the lease ends; longer for month-to-month tenancies and in rent-controlled areas.
Can I raise rent on renewal?
Yes, subject to local rent control, notice requirements and any rent-cap ordinances.
Is a verbal renewal binding?
Usually no — multi-month leases over a year generally need to be in writing under the statute of frauds.
What if the tenant stays without signing?
They typically become a holdover or month-to-month tenant under the existing terms, per local law.

title: Lease Termination Agreement | Free Word Template
description: Free mutual lease termination agreement: end a tenancy early with a signed move-out date, deposit terms and release.
lead: A signed agreement between landlord and tenant to end a lease early on agreed terms — move-out date, rent owed, security deposit handling, and mutual release.
introParagraphs: A lease termination agreement (or mutual move-out agreement) lets a landlord and tenant end a fixed-term lease early by mutual consent instead of eviction or abandonment. It sets the final move-out date, who pays what, and releases both sides from further obligations.

Use this when the tenant wants to leave early and the landlord agrees, or when both sides want a clean break. It is cleaner than breaking the lease unilaterally because it waives future rent claims in writing.
bullets: Parties and property
Landlord and tenant names, property address, original lease start and end dates.
Termination date
The agreed date the tenancy ends and keys are returned.
Final rent and fees
How much rent is owed through termination, any early-termination fee (where legal), and when it is paid.
Security deposit
How the deposit will be handled, itemised deductions, timeline for return per local law.
Mutual release
Language releasing both parties from future claims under the lease, except for post-move-out damages not covered here.
howTo: Agree on terms verbally
Discuss move-out date, final rent and deposit disposition before drafting.
Put it in writing
Use the agreement to capture dates, amounts and release terms.
Sign and date
Both landlord and tenant sign; each gets a copy.
Complete move-out
Tenant vacates, returns keys, and completes a walkthrough inspection on or before the termination date.
Return the deposit
Landlord returns deposit less lawful deductions within the statutory window (commonly 21-30 days).
related: One-sided termination notice when no mutual agreement is reached.
If the alternative is extending rather than ending.
Court-stage option when the tenant will not leave.
faq: Do I have to sign a termination agreement?
No — if both sides do not agree, the lease terms and local law govern how either party can end it.
Can the landlord keep the deposit?
Only for lawful deductions (unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear) within the statutory timeframe.
Does it waive back rent?
That depends on what you write in the agreement. It can release past unpaid rent or require payment.
Is an early-termination fee legal?
Generally yes if it is a reasonable estimate of losses — some states cap fees or require specific language.
What if the tenant does not move out on the agreed date?
The agreement is breached — you would typically proceed with eviction per local law.

title: Rent Increase Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free rent increase letter template: formal notice to a tenant of a rent change with proper notice and effective date.
lead: A formal written notice to a tenant that the monthly rent will increase, stating the new amount, effective date, and required response/acceptance.
introParagraphs: A rent increase letter formally notifies a tenant that their rent is going up, typically at lease renewal or on a month-to-month tenancy. It states the new amount, effective date, and how to accept (by signing or continuing to pay) or decline (by giving notice to vacate).

Rent increases are heavily regulated. Most jurisdictions require 30-90 days written notice before the increase takes effect, and rent-controlled areas cap how much you can raise and when. Check local rules before sending.
bullets: Tenant and property
Tenant name, unit and property address, current rent amount.
New rent
New monthly rent amount and the effective date.
Notice period
How many days notice is given (matching local law — often 30, 60 or 90 days).
Reason or context (if required)
Some jurisdictions require a stated reason or CPI justification; most do not.
Response
How to accept (sign and return, or simply pay the new amount) and what happens if they decline (move-out by a set date).
howTo: Check local rules
Confirm allowable increase amount and required notice period — rent control applies in many cities.
Set the effective date
Make sure the date is at least the full notice period out and, for fixed leases, tied to renewal.
Draft the letter
State the current and new rent, effective date, and response deadline.
Deliver per law
Send via the method required (certified mail, hand delivery, posting) and keep proof of service.
Process the response
If tenant signs, keep the signed copy; if they decline, plan for their move-out or follow non-renewal procedures.
related: Often sent together when renewing a fixed-term lease.
If the tenant pays the old amount after increase, a pay-or-quit notice may be needed.
If the tenant does not accept the new rent, end the tenancy.
Update the lease to reflect new rent.
faq: How much can I raise rent?
In non-rent-controlled areas, generally any amount with proper notice; rent-controlled areas cap annual increases (e.g. CPI + a fixed percentage).
How much notice is required?
Typically 30 days for increases under 10% and 60 days for increases over 10% in many US states; check your local law.
Can I raise rent in the middle of a lease?
Usually no — fixed-term locks rent for the term unless the lease allows an increase with notice.
Can the tenant refuse?
Yes — they can give notice to vacate instead of paying the new rent.
Email enough?
Most jurisdictions require written notice via certified mail or hand delivery for rent increases; email may not count.

title: Security Deposit Return Letter | Free Word Template
h1: Free security deposit return letter template (Word)
description: Free security deposit return letter: itemised deductions and refund statement after a tenant moves out.
lead: A letter from the landlord to the tenant returning the security deposit (less itemised deductions for unpaid rent, cleaning, or damages beyond normal wear) after move-out.
introParagraphs: A security deposit return letter (or itemised deduction statement) is sent to a tenant after move-out, returning whatever portion of their deposit is not being withheld, along with a detailed list of deductions. Most US states require this within 14-30 days of move-out, and many impose penalties (double or triple damages) if you miss the deadline or fail to itemise.
Deductions must be for unpaid rent, cleaning to restore the unit to move-in condition, or damage beyond normal wear and tear — not for ordinary wear from living in the property.
bullets: Tenant and property
Former tenant names, forwarding address, property address and unit, move-out date.
Original deposit
Amount originally paid and date received.
Itemised deductions
List each deduction with category (unpaid rent, cleaning, repairs, key replacement, etc.) and the amount.
Refund amount
The net amount being returned (deposit minus deductions).
Payment method and deadline
How the refund is sent (cheque, transfer), enclosure, and the legal deadline being met.
howTo: Do a move-out walkthrough
Compare condition to the move-in inspection report; photograph damage.
Collect invoices
Get actual repair/cleaning receipts — lump-sum estimates may not hold up in court.
Itemise deductions
List each deduction with a short description and cost; withhold only lawful categories.
Calculate the refund
Deposit minus total deductions; return the balance.
Send on time
Mail to the tenant forwarding address within the statutory window (e.g. 21 or 30 days), with proof of mailing.
related: Mutual move-out agreement before sending this letter.
The notice period that precedes move-out.
Provide receipts for final rent paid.
Deposit terms from the original lease.
faq: How long do I have to return the deposit?
14-60 days depending on the state — most common is 21 or 30 days after move-out/key return.
What can I deduct?
Unpaid rent, cleaning beyond normal wear, damages beyond normal wear, key replacement — not ordinary wear.
Do I need receipts?
Many states require you to provide invoices/receipts for deductions on request; attach them to be safe.
What if I miss the deadline?
In many states you forfeit the right to withhold anything and the tenant can sue for double or triple damages.
Can I deduct for repainting?
Only for damage beyond normal wear — repainting after a long tenancy is normal wear in most places.

title: Landlord Reference Letter | Free Word Template
description: Free landlord reference letter template: confirm tenancy, rent history and conduct for a tenant applying elsewhere.
lead: A letter from a current or former landlord to a prospective landlord confirming the tenant rental history, on-time rent payments, and conduct.
introParagraphs: A landlord reference letter (or tenant reference) is written by a past or current landlord for a tenant who is applying for a new rental. It confirms tenancy dates, monthly rent, whether rent was paid on time, any issues, and whether you would rent to them again.

Stick to factual information (dates, rent amounts, late payments, damage, noise complaints) and avoid protected-class statements (race, religion, family status, disability) that can expose you to fair-housing liability.
bullets: Tenant and property
Tenant name(s), rental address and unit, tenancy start and end dates.
Rent history
Monthly rent amount, whether it was paid on time, number of late payments or NSF cheques if any.
Conduct and care
Whether the tenant kept the unit in good condition, followed lease rules, had noise or neighbour complaints, pets as allowed.
Security deposit
Whether the deposit was returned in full or with deductions (briefly).
Recommendation
Whether you would rent to this tenant again (yes/no/with conditions) and a contact number for verification.
howTo: Verify the request
Confirm the prospective landlord identity before sharing tenant information.
Gather facts
Check your rent ledger for late payments; review move-in/move-out condition reports.
Stick to facts
State dates, rent, payment record and conduct objectively; skip personal opinions and protected-class references.
Sign and date
Sign the letter and include contact information for follow-up calls.
Send it to the requester
Send directly to the prospective landlord (give a copy to the tenant only if appropriate).
related: Proof of income often requested alongside a landlord reference.
Where references are collected from applicants.
Lease the tenant is applying for.
faq: Am I required to write a reference?
Generally no — unless an agreement or local law requires it. You can politely decline.
Can I say negative things?
Only factual, documented truths (late rent, eviction filings, property damage). False statements can lead to defamation claims.
Can I charge for it?
Some jurisdictions allow a small administrative fee; check local rules.
What about co-tenants?
Reference the named tenants you actually rented to — avoid commenting on occupants not on the lease.
How long should it be?
One page is standard; include dates, rent, payment record and a clear recommendation line.
